title: Warming contrasts in legume share of grass and legume biomass were uncertain in four Cedar Creek samples in 2017-2022
abstract: We tested whether warming raised legume share within recorded legume-plus-grass biomass. This removes forb biomass from the denominator. We used 432 annual harvest records from two planting groups and two periods at Cedar Creek in 2017-2022. Four paired plot tests gave positive point bounds from 0.0146 to 0.1213 share units. All corrected outer intervals included zero. Five records had no focal biomass; bounds allow any share for these undefined responses. In four-species plots, the six-year descriptive sign could change when samples with focal biomass at most 2.5 percent were left unresolved. That sensitivity did not change the 16-species bounds. The records do not establish a repeated warming increase or a biological mechanism. One site, moving harvest strips, few plots and relative biomass limit inference. Code, aggregate results, hashes and external retrieval instructions support reproduction.

display.caption: Paired warming contrasts in recorded legume share of legume-plus-grass biomass. Thick lines bound undefined shares; thin lines include corrected plot uncertainty. All four intervals include zero.
